descriptions.text: Reentrancy. Lack of reentrancy lock for the flashloan()/deposit() functions, which was used by the hacker to manipulate the share price of LSWUSDC Vulnerable code snippet: Attack tx: https://snowtrace.io/tx/0xc6fb8217e45870a93c25e2098f54f6e3b24674a3083c30664867de474bf0212d Analysis: https://twitter.com/PeckShieldAlert/status/1606276020276891650

On December 23, Defrost Finance V2, the Avalanche ecological native stablecoin project, was attacked by a flash loan, and the hackers made a profit of $173,000. On December 25th, Defrost Finance V1 went wrong again, hackers managed to steal the owner’s key, the protocol was added with fake collateral tokens, and a malicious price oracle was used to liquidate current users, with losses estimated at more than $12 million. On December 27, the hackers who carried out the attack on Defrost Finance V1 have returned the stolen funds.

Defrost Finance on Avalanche suffered a two-stage December 2022 incident. A verified V2 reentrancy exploit on 2022-12-23 extracted about $173,000, and later disclosures said an owner-key-controlled V1 path with fake collateral and a malicious oracle drained roughly $12 million before funds were reportedly returned. V2 allowed reentry through the flash-loan and deposit path, which let the attacker manipulate LSWUSDC share accounting. V1 exposed owner-level collateral and oracle control powerful enough to register a worthless asset and liquidate positions against a fabricated price. The exact way the owner key was obtained remains unknown.
